role.altitude: The furnace operator keeps watching the process, adjusting controls, sampling and testing, and solving problems with colleagues; walking gauge rounds to write readings, counting output, copying setpoints and mailing fault details shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading process values and alarms on the control screen
role.ambitious_version: An operator whose rounds go to watching the process, not writing numbers down.

tasks.short: Read local gauges on rounds, watch equipment operation, product and panel lights, adjust controls when values drift and note deviations to monitor equipment operation and detect deviations from standards.

steps.what: Operator walks rounds to read local gauges for temperature, pressure and flow
Operator watches equipment operation, panel lights and product for deviations from standards
Operator adjusts controls when values drift
Operator notes deviations on the round sheet

tasks.design: Transmitters on the main local gauges send temperature, pressure and flow to the control screen, with fixed alarm limits per product. The operator sees those values and alarms from the panel and walks fewer gauge-reading rounds. Watching equipment, panel lights and product, adjusting controls and noting deviations stay with the operator. The alarms are fixed limits, not learning models, and do not replace any safety function.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local gauges could only be read on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Low-cost transmitters linked to the control system with fixed alarm limits.
tasks.still_hard: Old kilns with no free connection points.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a burner sound wrong before any gauge moves.
tasks.altitude: Fewer gauge rounds; watching the process stays.

evidence.claim: Machine data and tablet forms can go straight into the production system.
Learning models in safety functions need third-party conformity assessment from 14 January 2027, so alarms here are fixed limits.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring equipment; recording readings in log books (task 4965) is in this set and a separate task.
s4 is part of recording readings and production in log books, which task 4965 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: about 60% of gauges get transmitters; s1 is priced at that share.
Watching, adjusting and noting keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of local gauges per furnace.

incremental.description: Operator checks transmitter values against the gauge once a shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few gauges with transmitters; high: most gauges connected.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report malfunctions to supervisors in person or by radio, work with colleagues on production problems at the equipment, write fault notes, mail fault details to maintenance planning and check alarm history to confer about equipment malfunctions and production problems.

steps.what: Operator reports equipment malfunctions to supervisors in person or by radio
Operator works with other equipment operators to resolve production problems
Operator enters the fault report for maintenance
Operator mails fault details again to maintenance planning
Operator checks the alarm history on the control screen

tasks.design: In s3 the operator enters the fault on a tablet form that raises a work order in the maintenance system, instead of a paper note followed by a mail with the same details. Reporting to supervisors, solving problems with colleagues and checking alarms stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults were written on paper and mailed again.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet fault forms linked to the maintenance system.
tasks.still_hard: Faults that need a conversation to describe.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which colleague has seen this fault before.

evidence.claim: Tablet forms straight into the production or maintenance system replace paper and mail.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring about malfunctions; directing crane operators (task 4978) is a sibling task.
s3 keeps its time because a tablet form takes about as long as a paper note; s4 saves mailing the same details.
Talking and problem solving keep their full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few faults; high: many faults per shift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk to gauges to read values, take samples and run tests, count shift production, record gauge readings and test results in log books, write shift production and remarks and check the previous shift's log.

steps.what: Operator walks to gauges and reads values for the log
Operator takes samples and runs product tests
Operator counts shift production
Operator records gauge readings and test results in log books
Operator writes shift production and remarks in the log book
Operator checks the previous shift's log

tasks.design: Transmitters on the main gauges write readings to the process historian, and production counters on the line count output. The electronic shift log fills those values per hour, instead of the operator walking to read them and writing them down. The operator enters test results and remarks on a tablet. Sampling and testing stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every reading and count was walked, read and written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Transmitters, line counters and electronic shift logs.
tasks.still_hard: Visual readings such as colour that no sensor gives.
tasks.human_edge: Writing the remark that explains why a reading looks odd.
tasks.altitude: Less walking and writing; testing stays.

reach.learn: Whether logs are complete and on time.

evidence.claim: Logs of instrument readings and operational data on forms can be filled by machine data and tablet forms.
Per-operator production logs can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: recording readings, tests and production; calculating material amounts (task 4972) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: about half the logged gauges get transmitters; s1 is priced at that share and the rest stays a walk.
Input contract for s3: production counters on about half the lines; s3 is priced at that share.
s4 and s5 keep half or more for test results and remarks typed on the tablet.
The works council consents before logs are kept per operator.

incremental.description: Operator checks the auto-filled log at the end of the shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few connected gauges; high: most gauges and lines connected.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive instructions at handover, check material and equipment against the order, read and interpret work orders and process specifications, look up recipe settings, enter setpoints, check the schedule and ask planning about changes to determine work assignments, process specifications and production schedules.

steps.what: Operator receives instructions at the shift handover
Operator checks material and equipment against the work order at the furnace
Operator reads and interprets work orders and process specifications
Operator looks up recipe settings in the specification binder and copies them to the setpoint sheet
Operator enters setpoints into the furnace controller
Operator checks the production schedule spreadsheet
Operator asks planning about schedule changes by mail

tasks.design: Recipe setpoints per product are kept in the production system and loaded to the furnace controller with the work order, and the operator confirms them on the screen. This replaces looking them up in a binder, copying them to a sheet and typing them in. Handover, checking material, reading orders, the schedule and questions to planning stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setpoints were copied from binders and typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Recipe management in production systems with download to controllers.
tasks.still_hard: Older controllers with no download link.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that this batch of material needs a slower ramp.
tasks.altitude: Less copying settings; reading the job stays.

evidence.claim: A production system computes recipe parameters by business rules.

assumptions: Boundary: reading work orders and instructions; calculating material amounts (task 4972) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4 and s5: about 60% of furnaces have controllers that accept a recipe download; s4 and s5 are priced near that share.
Recipe download is deterministic and not a safety function.
Handover, material checks, reading and planning questions keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of product changes per shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few product changes; high: many changes per shift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
